prompt:
Research what the Python Software Foundation or the CPython developers have officially said about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build. Cite the PEP or documentation page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here is what the Python Software Foundation and CPython developers have officially stated about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build, drawn directly from accepted PEPs, official documentation, and Steering Council announcements.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build has additional overhead when executing Python code compared to the default GIL-enabled build." | CLAIM: Free-threaded builds inherently incur execution overhead compared to standard GIL-enabled builds.
SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: Single-threaded performance overhead varies by hardware, currently ranging from 1% to 8% on standard benchmarks.
SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build will typically use more memory compared to the default build." | CLAIM: Free-threaded builds require more memory than default GIL-enabled builds.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The changes to make CPython thread-safe without the GIL increase execution overhead for `--disable-gil` builds." | CLAIM: The fundamental architectural changes required for thread-safety without the GIL increase execution overhead.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "Note that this PEP would not affect the performance of the default (non `--disable-gil`) builds of CPython." | CLAIM: Disabling the GIL and the associated overhead are entirely isolated to the free-threaded build and do not impact the performance of standard CPython builds.
SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "The performance impact should be isolated to a free-threaded build; a GIL build should not see any performance impact in existing code." | CLAIM: The Steering Council requires that performance impacts remain strictly confined to the free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "At this point we’re expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council officially anticipates a worst-case performance penalty of 10-15% for the free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "the performance penalty on linear performance, comparing a free-threaded build against a with-GIL build, as measured by the pyperformance benchmarks... is currently around 10% (except on macOS, where it’s more like 3%)." | CLAIM: Current linear performance penalty is around 10% on Linux/Windows and 3% on macOS.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)." | CLAIM: The current memory overhead for free-threaded Python is approximately 15-20%.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "Realistically, though, higher memory use is the cost of having efficient, safe free-threading, and we are unlikely to get this very close to the with-GIL build’s memory use without significant performance cost." | CLAIM: Higher memory usage is an accepted, inherent trade-off for efficient and safe free-threading.
